concerns.text: The validation target (WALS typological feature differences) is not independent of the predictor (shift vectors derived from language‑specific token frequency distributions). Both the shift vectors (computed as W_U^{+} × f) and the WALS features are driven by the same underlying language‑specific token frequencies, making the correlation analysis circular and guaranteeing a non‑trivial relationship by construction.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 1 – Model Loading & Edge Spectrum Extraction
concerns.text: Edge‑spectrum subspaces are extracted per model, not per language. Yet the plan measures “cosine similarity between edge‑spectrum bases across model‑language pairs”, conflating model differences with language differences. Since the edge spectrum is a property of the model’s unembedding matrix (trained on multilingual data), it is not inherently language‑specific, so this comparison does not validly test the hypothesis of a universal vs. language‑specific prior.

The plan treats the edge‑spectrum similarity metric and the mean‑embedding shift metric as independent predictors, but both are derived from the same unembedding matrix W_U. This violates the assumption that validation targets must be independent of the predictors, potentially inflating apparent effects and undermining the statistical interpretation of subsequent correlation and permutation tests.
